I haven't seen it, so I cannot comment on that. Overall, how do you feel about the game? The  
first half, you made some decent chances and  one very good one early in the second, but  
then it kind of petered out, and you struggled.  How did you feel about your attacking output?
What I feel—very disappointing not  to win the game because, obviously,  
if there's a team that deserves to win,  there is only one, which is Arsenal. 
We did nothing, we gave nothing away—no shots  conceded. Dominated the play, didn’t allow  
them to run, no set pieces. High press—excellent. We had to track back—excellent. We got them there,  
we generated the chances, but the last 20 minutes  was missing to score goals, which is what you  
have to do with all the dominance because we  have never been able to dominate in that way. 
But at the end, you have to try  to generate the highest winning  
probability. We slightly done that. Now that you draw the game,  
you want more—even if we win it, we always  want more. But I cannot ask much more of the  
boys apart from putting the ball in the net. Can you talk us through the substitutions?
With Declan, I had to take him out  because he was feeling something. 
With Martin, it was a tactical  decision to try to change their  
rhythm, especially on that side. It wasn’t a fitness decision?
No, no. Have you  
seen the Liverpool score now? Does it feel like  even more of a disappointment to drop points?
Yeah, I'm very disappointed because when  you do what we’ve done today against them,  
you have to win the game, you know. But, at the end, this is football. It is the  
hardest thing—those last 20-25 minutes—to do what  we have to do. Credit to them as well: how they  
blocked shots, to Pickford for the saves that he's  made, the way they desire that they defend with. 
But, honestly, it’s difficult to  ask something else of the team. 
Individually, can we do things a little bit  better and deliver more quality and deliver the  
magic moment in that case that is necessary?  Yes, but that’s something that is not easy.
Are those magic moments  coachable, or is that difficult?
At the end, you need the spark, and you need to  be precise. I mean, we had the chances—this could  
have been 2-3-0—and nobody’s talking about it. The reality is 0-0, and they're not going to  
talk about all the incredible things  that the team did in the game. 
I mean, certainly it is not energy.  When I see my team track back,  
it’s unbelievable. Every three days, 70  minutes, all the team is going there.
So very difficult to ask them  something else because they want it. 
There were a few moments in the second half  when you seemed to be demanding more from  
fans behind you. You didn’t seem particularly  happy from what we saw. What was going on?
What it is, is that we have to manage the  frustration and the time because if not, we  
start to speed up the game when there is no room  to speed it up, and we start to rush the game. 
And we need to understand that—no,  we start to force, to make mistakes,  
and to lose the grip of the game, and  we have to stay very far away from that. 
Do fans need to understand that too and  not express it? Is that what you mean?
No, no. Well, I cannot ask the fans to understand.  I’m telling you what my feeling is tactically. 
Maybe some people were surprised taking off  the main attacking threat. Do you feel like  
the lack of chances in the last 20-30 minutes,  in hindsight, could you have kept him on?
I understand. If Eddie comes in and scores  the goal, it’s a great option. If he doesn’t,  
you have taken your captain out. That’s football. What was Martin’s reaction coming off?
Well, the same reaction as Martinelli—everybody.  I’m sure that they want to continue to play the  
90 minutes. But that’s why we have  the options to try to help the team. 
Just on Declan, is there any idea  what the issue exactly is and how bad?
No, he’s been with a little niggle for  the last week or so, and he had to be  
subbed in that moment, so we had to do it. Three consecutive games without scoring from  
open play in the Premier League—how  much of a concern is that for you?
In the Premier League? Yeah, but we scored  three from open play three days ago. 
So you’re not worried that  continuing might impact?
Obviously, it won’t continue. We score goals,  we have the chances like we have done today  
again, and I’m sure we will score. The problem is that if we don’t... 
Fábio Vieira got a question, gave him chances, and  if he keeps grabbing them the way he’s done today  
again, because I think he was really good, he will  continue to have chances because he deserves it.
title: Mikel Arteta Post Match Press Conference | Arsenal 0-0 Everton
